title: Replicate the f33v and f93r sunflower comparisons with independent annotators
statement: These are separate published proposals. A caption-masked comparison against ten botanical prints found three of four head features in common between f93r and Dodoens's sunflower. Gerard's sunflower agrees in eight of twelve features with f93r, with two uncertain. Fuchs's teasel agrees in nine of twelve with none uncertain. Neither sunflower print agrees in more than four known features with f33v. The two Voynich drawings and the proposals were known when I planned the comparison. I also prepared the cards and supplied the only ratings. The packet records the individual features, crop bounds, open witnesses and ambiguities.
check: Recruit two annotators who have not seen the scoring key. Give them the twelve-feature checklist and random caption-free crops of all eight controls and both sunflower witnesses, together with the Yale f33v and f93r figure crops. Have them score the regions independently, record ambiguities, and publish their individual scores before revealing identities. Add independent period prints of both sunflowers and comparable Old World plants before any claim of specificity. Require a separate agreed link between the illustration and a discrete manuscript string before proposing an anchor.
record:
# Two sunflower proposals, two different figures

Ardıç proposes a sunflower on f33v. Stolfi's institutional note compares f33v with sunflower, including leaf attachment and the round underground objects, and prefers another possibility. Janick's published sunflower iconography reproduces **f93r**, cites O'Neill's earlier proposal and describes the single stalk and large seed head with suggestions of rays. These are two different folios. The claims are documented in the open [Ardıç companion](https://www.turkicresearch.com/Research/SubPages/Voynich), [Stolfi note](https://www.ic.unicamp.br/en/~stolfi/EXPORT/voynich/98-01-17-sunflower/) and [Janick 2020, pp. 1123–1125, figs. 9 and 11](https://www.notulaebotanicae.ro/index.php/nbha/article/download/12015/8986/48289).

## Scans and method

[Beinecke f33v](https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/oid/2002046/canvas/1006139) and [Beinecke f93r](https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/oid/2002046/canvas/1006238) are the public target scans. Load the corresponding Yale IIIF image IDs at 1200 px wide. The botanical cards are public-domain historical illustrations, shown by open sites. The Dodoens sunflower and both Voynich targets were known before the rubric. I fixed the eight control categories and twelve binary features before viewing the newly sourced prints. I prepared the crops, saw the full pages while doing so, and scored the shuffled grayscale cards. Masking removed the captions from the comparison views. My visual recognition and memory of the sources could still affect the scores. The work has one observer.

Features apply to the drawings as depicted. The head criteria are a densely patterned central field, distinct peripheral blades at least a quarter of the field's transverse width, a rounded outline of that field as opposed to a tapered silhouette, and a single terminal head on the plant. Buds on separate terminals count as evidence of multiple heads. In a spray of separate flowers without a shared field, the first three criteria are uncertain. Leaves are scored for a broad blade, obvious lobes or divisions, at least three major ridges spreading radially, an illustrated stalk–blade join visibly inside the margin, and a repeated opposite or near-opposite arrangement. Roots are scored for an exposed drawing below the stem join, many thin filaments and bounded round bulbs or knots. Compare agreement on known features and retain all uncertain comparisons. Color, relative figure size and dates carry no score.

The Yale f33v head fields are oval despite their perspective. The pale central marks on its leaves hint at a center attachment. The painted overlap makes the exact join and radial ridges uncertain. The three round objects visibly connect to branching underground strands. The dotted head on f93r has a tapered outline and short marginal strokes under the blade-length criterion. Its near-paired leaves are smooth curved arcs. The root join opens into many thin filaments. The paler form near the manuscript text was excluded as possible show-through.

## Outcome

Each cell below is **agreements / disagreements / uncertain**. The per-feature table gives the underlying observations.

| C02 sunflower | 2/2/0 | 3/5/4 | 3/1/0 | 6/4/2 |
| C03 castor | 1/0/3 | 5/1/6 | 0/1/3 | 3/5/4 |

| C05 sunflower | 2/1/1 | 4/4/4 | 2/1/1 | 8/2/2 |

| C10 artichoke | 0/0/4 | 4/2/6 | 0/0/4 | 5/3/4 |

For f33v, several controls achieve three known head agreements, where both sunflower plates achieve two. Castor agrees on the broad divided leaves, and navelwort shares one rounded root knot. Neither control depicts the specific combination of three disks, deep broad lobes and multiple ray-like heads. For f93r, Dodoens has three known head agreements (dense field, short fringe, one terminal head) but the field is rounded rather than tapered. Gerard shows the exposed filaments and eight overall agreements. Teasel agrees in nine overall, with two known head disagreements (rounded and multiple). If both uncertain Gerard comparisons are scored as matches, its score rises to ten. These rankings depend on the witness and on which body region is compared.

The panel is small and targeted. Most controls are from one herbal and the two sunflower images and Voynich drawings are from different book traditions. The counts describe the selected pictures, with no sampling inference or date estimate. Neither picture yielded a species-specific identifying combination on the observed features. This experiment offers no word–picture pairing.

ratings.note: Two fully exposed scale fields and a partly hidden third. Pale central marks suggest axial attachment but painted overlap prevents tracing it. Three separate round disks on sparsely branching roots.
Dotted tapered head with short marginal strokes. Broad smooth arcs in near pairs and many bare thin strands below the join.
Patterned mature head plus a bud. Basal lamina joins, one dominant curved root.
Patterned oval head and short narrow edge. Soil line without an exposed root system.
Separate fruit and flower spikes. Star-shaped broad blades, center attachments and mostly thick branching roots.
Two heads with radially spreading blades and no clearly textured central field. Narrow leaves and thin rootlets off one axis.
Dense rounded disc. Overlapping exterior leaf and head margins complicate blade lengths and leaf joints. Exposed thin roots.
Multiple rounded heads. Repeated long blades, low detail center and thin fibrous roots.
Basal rosette with several long-stemmed heads. Center detail uncertain at this scale.
Several clusters of separate small flowers. Several leaves appear attached inside the margin. A round basal knot with many filaments.
Many oval textured heads with spines rather than blades. Clearly paired leaves and many slender branches below the root join.
Reproductive head not depicted. Deep divisions follow one axis per blade. Dominant long roots with sparse thin branches and no round knot.
